Concentrated finding round (unified triage seat, 2026-08-17): **promoted to `pm:queue`**, type `Bug`. Seat-graded rather than escalated: a published entry that plain Node ESM cannot load is strictly worse than one it can, fixing the emit changes no API and costs an emit setting — "obvious problems get fixed directly." Scope: make the `@object-ui/react` build emit extensioned relative specifiers (build/emit setting), and add the smoke check the card sketches (import each published entry under plain Node) so the property holds repo-wide rather than per-package — if the smoke check turns up other packages with the same emission, fix or ledger them in the same PR, stating which. Premise check at claim: confirm the current dist still emits extensionless specifiers. S–M / opus.

Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — path tier derived this round: no mandate; judgement tier for a packaging change with a repo-wide check attached.
Clause-②: no — the published export set is unchanged. This makes an already-declared entry *loadable*; it neither widens the public face nor moves the accept set.
Serial constraints cleared: `packages/react` is free — no open PR touches it, and the three retained cards occupy `app-shell` and `components`/`fields`. The smoke check is new-file work.

## Zone 1 — Triage's ruling (binding)

Promoted to `pm:queue`, type `Bug`, seat-graded: a published entry plain Node ESM cannot load is strictly worse than one it can, and fixing it changes no API. Scope: make `@object-ui/react` load under plain Node, **and** add the smoke check that actually *imports* each published entry — the card is right that a check stopping at resolution would not have caught this. If the smoke check turns up other packages with the same emission, fix or ledger them in the same PR, stating which.

## ⛔ Zone 2 — the ruling's stated fix shape is probably WRONG. Verify before you build.

Triage scoped this as "a build/emit setting". **I measured it this round and I do not think such a setting exists here.** Treat the following as a mechanism assumption to confirm or refute — refuting it is a good outcome, silently building the wrong fix is not:

- `packages/react/package.json` → `"build": "tsc"`. Plain `tsc`, no bundler.
- **TypeScript does not rewrite import specifiers.** There is no emit flag that appends `.js` to relative specifiers. What is in the source is what lands in `dist`.
- The source already carries them extensionless — `packages/react/src/index.ts:9–18`: `export * from './SchemaRenderer'`, `'./hooks'`, `'./context'`, `'./LazyPluginLoader'`, `'./spec-bridge'`, `'./data-invalidation'`. These are exactly the specifiers the card observed failing in `dist`.
- Nothing complains today because the **root** `tsconfig.json` sets `"moduleResolution": "bundler"` (with `"module": "ESNext"`), which permits extensionless relative specifiers. `packages/react/tsconfig.json` extends the root and does not override it.

So the fix is a **source-specifier change**, and the durable version pairs it with a per-package `moduleResolution` (`nodenext`/`node16`) so the compiler *rejects* a missing extension and the property cannot silently regress. Declared = enforced beats a fix that holds only until the next import is written.

**⛔ Hard constraint: do not change `moduleResolution` in the ROOT `tsconfig.json`.** 38 packages extend it; flipping it repo-wide is a different, much larger card and is not authorised here. Override inside `packages/react` only. If you conclude the property genuinely cannot be enforced without a root change, **stop and report** — that is a fork, not something to force.

## The check has to load, not resolve

The card's sharpest measured point, and the acceptance bar: `plugin-charts`' own entry is clean, and the failure only appears once evaluation crosses **into** `@object-ui/react`. A per-package check that stops at resolution passes while the tree is broken. Your smoke check must actually evaluate each published entry under plain Node. A green run that never imported anything is the failure mode I will look for on review.

## Premise check first (triage asked for this explicitly)

Build and confirm the current `dist` still emits extensionless specifiers before fixing anything. This card is from 2026-08-13; if the emission has since changed, `premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is a **legitimate and useful delivery** — report the measurement, do not manufacture a diff to justify the dispatch.

## Gates

Derive from your diff — expect `Lint`, `Type Check`, the test shards, changeset gates, plus whatever CI job you wire the smoke check into. Re-derive against what you actually changed and run the families you touch. Changeset required; if you touch other packages' build configs, each needs one.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #4538`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report **and** post it as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`. Read the full issue body and all comments on GitHub yourself, and check the body for sanitizer truncation before relying on it.

Claim-surface amendment (session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`, branch `claude/issue-4538-react-esm-loadable`)

Declaring an addition to the file surface in the claim above, in the same round, before the PR opens.

**Declared:** `packages/react/src/**`, `packages/react/tsconfig.json`, the new check plus its CI wiring.
**Added:** `packages/types/src/**`, `packages/core/src/**`, `packages/i18n/src/**` — specifier text only, no build-config or API change in any of the three.

## Why the addition was forced rather than chosen

Fixing `packages/react` alone did **not** make its entry loadable. After the 92 specifiers in `packages/react/src` were extensioned and the package rebuilt clean, the entry still failed — one package over, exactly the asymmetry the card is about:

```
FAILED ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
Cannot find module '.../packages/i18n/dist/i18n'
  imported from '.../packages/i18n/dist/index.js'
```

`@object-ui/react` evaluates into `types` (11 extensionless), `core` (11) and `i18n` (55), each a bare-`tsc` build carrying the identical defect. Stopping at the declared surface would have produced a PR that changes 92 specifiers and leaves the card's own acceptance bar — the entry loads under plain Node — still failing. After the three were fixed:

```
LOADED+EVALUATED OK — named exports: 142
```

The four conditions for a bounded in-place fix all hold: same defect class; mechanical, with the correct shape already pinned by what `packages/react` proved; no open PR touches `types`/`core`/`i18n` (checked against the open PR list); same gate family, no new verification surface.

## What I did NOT extend to

The seven other packages that carry this defect — `app-shell` (1259 specifiers), `fields` (295), `auth` (54), `mobile` (27), `collaboration` (15), `permissions` (14), `providers` (9) — are **ledgered, not fixed**, and filed as #5214. `app-shell` and `fields` are held by other sessions per the claim; the rest are outside the declared surface and are not required for this card's acceptance bar. Taking triage's "fix or ledger them in the same PR, stating which" as the ledger branch.

Root `tsconfig.json` is untouched. The `nodenext` override is scoped to `packages/react/tsconfig.json` only.

**ACCEPT** — PM review of record (seat `repo:objectui`, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`). PR #5218.

- **PR shape** — draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #4538`.
- **Scope** — path surface taken **from git** (`git diff --name-only origin/main...FETCH_HEAD`), not from the report: 69 files; packages touched are exactly `core`, `i18n`, `react`, `types`; non-src surfaces are the changeset, `ci.yml`, the new `node-esm-load-gate.yml`, `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`, root `package.json`, `packages/react/tsconfig.json`, and the new gate + its test. **`packages/app-shell` and `packages/fields` untouched** — the regions other sessions hold.
- **ACCEPT path fork** — **zero governed paths** (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), verified by pattern match over the full file list. Clean → lands through the queue.
- **CI** — 21 check runs, all `completed`: **19 success, 2 skipped, zero failures.** `Type Check` green is the load-bearing one: the `nodenext` override had to not break compilation across the four packages.
- **Changeset** — present, patch-scored, no-major gate green.

**What makes this a strong delivery rather than a passing one:**

1. **It refuted triage's framing with measurement, which is exactly what the dispatch asked for.** Triage scoped this as "a build/emit setting". The dev confirmed all four points of the Zone 2 assumption instead — bare `tsc`, no specifier rewriting, source-level defect, permitted by the root's `moduleResolution: bundler` — and fixed the source rather than hunting for a flag that does not exist. **It also correctly reported that no fork was needed**: the property was enforceable with a per-package override, so the ROOT `tsconfig.json` was never touched. That was the hard constraint and it held.
2. **The gate cannot be green over nothing.** The acceptance bar was that the check must *import and evaluate*, not resolve — because `plugin-charts`' own entry was always clean and the failure only appears once evaluation crosses into `@object-ui/react`. The load leg `import()`s each entry in a child `node` through its own `exports` map, **and asserts a floor on the count** (17 of 39 measured). "Imported nothing, found nothing" therefore cannot pass. That is the failure mode I said I would look for, closed deliberately.
3. **The scope extension was declared before it happened.** Fixing `packages/react` alone did not make its entry loadable — evaluation dies one package over in `i18n`. Extending to `types`/`core`/`i18n` (specifier text only, no build-config or API change) was posted as a claim-surface amendment on the issue **before** the PR opened, which is the protocol. I would have accepted a stop-and-report here too; declaring and proceeding was the better call and it was made the right way.
4. **Two false-criterion traps were caught and pinned** — grading the emit question on the build *command* produced 124 phantom findings against a package whose `tsc` step carries `noEmit: true`, and stripping comments before scanning shifted every finding by the six-line licence header. Both are now tests. A gate that reports confidently wrong line numbers is worse than no gate.
5. **The debt was ledgered, not swept.** Seven further packages carry the same emission (filed as #5214) and are left alone — `app-shell` and `fields` because other sessions hold them, the rest because they are outside this card's bar. The ledger is a ratchet: an entry whose package has become clean is itself a failure, so it cannot outlive the debt. And `plugin-dashboard`/`plugin-map` are kept in a **separate** ledger because they fail on a third-party `.css` import that no extension fixes — refusing to let one gate become a grab-bag.

**Measured outcome:** the card's original repro now reads `OK @object-ui/plugin-charts — 6 exports` / `OK @object-ui/react — 142 exports`, against a premise that was re-confirmed failing (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on `dist/SchemaRenderer`) before any edit.

**Declared deviation, accepted:** the load leg runs nightly rather than per-PR, since this repo has no per-PR full-repo build — the same trade `published-dist-gate.yml` already records. The per-PR leg is the source scan, which needs no build and is wired into `Type Check`.

Flipping out of draft and enqueueing. I will confirm MERGED before this card leaves the in-flight set.
